title: Poverty Reduction
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Talk about poverty without pointing at anyone in class. Overexploitation: charcoal burning, overfishing, sand harvesting.

skills.key_step: The child names causes of poverty in Africa and explains how overexploiting resources deepens it.

floor.prerequisite: Gives the effects of high population density.
floor.question: Give one effect of high density.

steps: Say how it leads to poverty.

board.do: Draw a hill with many trees, then with stumps.

board.say: What happens to families who sold charcoal now?

misconceptions.ask: Which is a cause of poverty?
misconceptions.repair: Underline "un-" and ask what it changes.

misconceptions.ask: What can overexploiting resources lead to?
misconceptions.repair: Show a forest cut for charcoal over five years in drawings.
Pair: corruption takes money from services; good governance uses it for people.

listen_for: No, only lazy people are poor
misconceptions.ask: Can a hardworking family be poor?
misconceptions.repair: Read a story of a farming family hit by drought.

checks.question: Give two causes of poverty in Africa.
checks.answer: any two of: unemployment, drought, corruption, conflict, low education, rapid population growth

checks.question: What can overexploiting resources lead to?
